answer: Give each identity standing only through cross-domain work. A newcomer starts with no weight and must earn contributions in three areas—code, review, and moderation—over several epochs. Weight decays when activity stops, so standing is like a falcon that must keep flying, not a badge once bought. An attacker pays a recurring cost per fake identity: each needs its own useful trail, and one operator cannot credibly sustain many trails at once. A harbor of audited records exposes cloned work, and decay stops abandoned identities being stockpiled like a hidden oasis for a sudden attack.
